title: Scalar extension of flat chain maps and their canonical derived transposes
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of commutative rings. Work on the small etale sites in ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact geometric inverse images $r_R^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ for derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $\lambda:T_Wr_A^*\cong r_B^*T_V$ for the inverse of the canonical normalized scalar/pullback isomorphism [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso].

Let $P$ be a cochain complex on $V$ and $K$ one on $W$, both K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and let $h:r_A^*P\to K$ be a chain map. Put $P_B=P\otimes_{A_V}B_V$ and $K_B=K\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ termwise. The canonical scalar-extension representatives identify $T_V(QP)$ with $QP_B$ and $T_W(QK)$ with $QK_B$. Let $\rho_P:r_B^*P_B\cong(r_A^*P)\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ be the ordinary scalar/pullback reassociation, and define $a_h=(h\otimes1)\rho_P$. Its degreewise ordinary $B$-adjuncts form a chain map $\pi_h:P_B\to r_{*,B}K_B$.

Under those specified flat-model and exact-pullback identifications, the morphism
$$m_h=T_W(Qh)\circ\lambda_{QP}^{-1}:r_B^*T_V(QP)\longrightarrow T_W(QK)$$
is represented by $a_h$, and its derived $B$-adjunct is
$$e_B^{-1}(m_h)=\alpha_{K_B}\circ Q(\pi_h),$$
where $e_B:\operatorname{Hom}(QP_B,Rr_{*,B}QK_B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(r_B^*QP_B,QK_B)$ and $\alpha$ are the canonical bijection and comparison [lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose]. Equivalently the right side has inverse transpose represented by $a_h$. These assertions are natural for pairs of chain maps $(u:P\to P',v:K\to K')$ satisfying $v h=h' r_A^*u$. No boundedness, properness, direct-image acyclicity or flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings): coefficient compatibility. Agent-written flat-chain transpose calculation, independent of properness and of direct-image acyclicity, using the scalar/pullback normalization and the canonical derived adjunction.

proof.text: Put $F_T(C)=C\otimes_{A_T}B_T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] to the constant-coefficient ringed-topos map associated to $r$ and to the identity-topos coefficient maps $A_T\to B_T$. It gives that $r_A^*P$, $P_B$ and $K_B$ are K-flat with flat terms over their respective rings, even for nonflat $A\to B$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the representative maps $\sigma_C:T_T(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF_T(C)$ are isomorphisms for $C=P,K,r_A^*P$. Their naturality in chain maps is the natural transformation in the left-derived universal property [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. The geometric pullbacks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and their canonical derived adjunction represents pullback termwise by [lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose]; use these fixed identifications throughout.

source.place: Tags 0G7E and 06YY: K-flat representatives and their canonical derived comparisons.

proof.text:
Write $c=\lambda^{-1}$, so that $c:r_B^*T_V\to T_Wr_A^*$. In the notation of [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], its ordinary comparison $a_P$ is precisely $\rho_P$. Substitute $f=r$ into that node's defining normalization. After the specified exact geometric representative identifications it reads
$$\sigma_{r_A^*P}\circ c_{QP}=Q(\rho_P)\circ r_B^*(\sigma_P).$$
All these representative maps are invertible by Step 1. Consequently, with source identified by $r_B^*(\sigma_P)$ and target by $\sigma_{r_A^*P}$, the particular canonical arrow $c_{QP}$ is represented by $\rho_P$. This uses the normalization equation itself, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the two functors.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 07A7: the defining scalar/pullback representative normalization.

proof.text:
Naturality of the representative transformation of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], for the chain map $h:r_A^*P\to K$, gives
$$\sigma_K\circ T_W(Qh)=Q(h\otimes1)\circ\sigma_{r_A^*P}.$$
Combine this with Step 2 and the definition $m_h=T_W(Qh)\circ c_{QP}$ to obtain
$$\sigma_K\circ m_h\circ(r_B^*\sigma_P)^{-1}
 =Q(h\otimes1)\circ Q(\rho_P)=Q((h\otimes1)\rho_P)=Q(a_h).$$
The ordinary scalar/pullback isomorphism is a chain isomorphism: its naturality with each differential gives $d\rho=\rho d$. Tensoring $h$ is a chain map since tensor is a functor. Thus $a_h$ is a chain map and this proves the asserted representative formula.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 07A4: naturality of representative maps and ordinary pullback/tensor reassociation.

proof.text: Let $b^0_{M,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(r_B^*M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_{*,B}N)$ be the ordinary module adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and define $\pi_h^n=b^0_{P_B^n,K_B^n}(a_h^n)$. The chain identity for $a_h$ is $d_{K_B}^n a_h^n=a_h^{n+1}r_B^*(d_{P_B}^n)$. Naturality of $b^0$ in its two variables sends its two sides to $r_{*,B}(d_{K_B}^n)\pi_h^n$ and $\pi_h^{n+1}d_{P_B}^n$, respectively. They are equal, so the degreewise adjuncts form a chain map. The inverse ordinary adjunction formula, degree by degree, gives $\varepsilon^0_{K_B}\circ r_B^*\pi_h=a_h$. There is no cohomology or direct-image acyclicity claim in this calculation.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), ordinary module adjunction and naturality.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose] with coefficient ring $R=B$, source complex $M=P_B$, target complex $K_B$, and chain map $f=\pi_h$. Its formula gives
$$e_B(\alpha_{K_B}\circ Q\pi_h)=Q(\varepsilon^0_{K_B}\circ r_B^*\pi_h)=Q(a_h).$$
The second equality is Step 4. Step 3 identifies this last arrow with $m_h$ under exactly the representative identifications in the statement. Since $e_B$ is a bijection, applying its inverse yields $e_B^{-1}(m_h)=\alpha_{K_B}\circ Q(\pi_h)$. The same displayed equality proves the equivalent inverse-transpose assertion. This cited result applies to arbitrary complexes, so $K_B$ need not be direct-image acyclic or K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility), with Tag 07A6: the canonical derived counit square.

proof.text:
For a pair $(u,v)$ as in the statement put $u_B=u\otimes1$ and $v_B=v\otimes1$. Naturality of $\rho$ gives $F_W(r_A^*u)\rho_P=\rho_{P'}r_B^*u_B$. Tensoring $vh=h'r_A^*u$ and composing with this equality gives
$$v_Ba_h=a_{h'}r_B^*u_B.$$
Ordinary adjunction naturality [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] therefore gives $r_{*,B}(v_B)\pi_h=\pi_{h'}u_B$. Localize and use naturality of $\alpha$ from [lem-sp-etale-derived-chain-transpose] to get
$$Rr_{*,B}(Qv_B)\alpha_{K_B}Q\pi_h=\alpha_{K'_B}Q\pi_{h'}Qu_B.$$
The naturality of that node's Hom bijection gives the matching equation for inverse transposes. Finally the scalar representatives are natural [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], and $c$ is a natural isomorphism [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], so the equations also hold before the representative identifications, for $m_h$ itself. This proves naturality in both variables.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the coefficient/mate compatibility behind det-sp-reduction-exceptional, through lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility and lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model: the flat-chain scalar/pullback and derived-adjunction calculation used in the proper coefficient model, without importing properness or acyclicity into this tool lemma.

tool_uses.why: General ringed-topos K-flat pullback preservation is applied to geometric pullback and identity-topos coefficient extension; this is a representative calculation, not a replacement of the unit coefficient route.
Only its specified natural left-derived comparison and invertibility on resolving representatives are used to compute a chain map after scalar extension.
Exact ordinary constant-coefficient geometric pullback and its module adjunction are the underlying algebraic tool for degreewise transposition.
General K-flat computation of derived change of coefficients supplies the canonical representatives on the three complexes.
